description: Native desktop UI components for Go, built on MyGo. Themed controls, window shells, Lucide icons, plus chat, Markdown, code highlighting, charts and a command palette. Also includes a standalone packager for macOS, Windows and Linux.
summary: Onevra is a native desktop UI kit for Go built on MyGo that hands you themed controls, a command palette, chat bubbles, Markdown rendering, and code highlighting without pulling in Electron or a Chromium runtime, which is the kind of local-first stack that fits how I think about shipping small tools. The cross-platform packager plus the clean separation where the app owns state, persistence, and async work means I could prototype a native front-end for PenguPool or AgentOn Pocket in an afternoon instead of wrestling with a web bridge. What sells me is the component contract: you compose shells and controls, the library doesn't try to become a framework, and the standard Go toolchain is all you need to keep it honest.
